about: A pilot's Start At descent in the nav log (the engine's navlog_with_descents, a leg marked start_at): it begins at the waypoint and runs on at three to one, 333 ft a nm (about the 3 degree glide path a VASI is normally set at, AIM 2-1-2), where Cross At has it done by the waypoint. Every leg is flown at 100 kt over the ground, 8 gal/h, on a course of 045 between the fixes AAA, Lake and BBB; each leg is [distance_nm, altitude_ft, start_at]. 2,000 ft at three to one is 6 nm, 3.6 min at 100 kt: 556 fpm, 550 to the nearest 50. Engine: engine/facade/tests/start_at_descents.rs. Not the web's: it never asks navlog_with_descents, the planner's nav log does, so the web's WebAssembly is built without it (scripts/build/web_rules.py). Down to a pattern the descent is finished where the 45-degree entry begins, 1.7236 nm from the field (the engine's pattern sketch: the downwind 0.75 sm out, the middle of FAA-H-8083-3C ch. 8's 1/2 to 1 mile, and a 1.2 nm entry to it at 45 degrees; AC 90-66C 11.2 and 11.3: at pattern altitude before entering), so a pattern's top of descent is 6 + 1.7236 nm before the field for 2,000 ft: 52.2764 nm along a 60 nm leg, 52.3 to the tenth, and 36 - 7.7236 x 0.6 = 31.37 min, 31.4.

cases.name: Cross At: the step down is done by the waypoint, 6 nm before it
Start At: the step down begins at the waypoint, the end of the leg into it
Start At, then down to a 1,500 ft pattern 6 nm before the 45-degree entry
Start At 6 nm from a 1,500 ft pattern: no room, so the descent to the pattern starts 12 nm before the 45-degree entry, before the waypoint
Start At a higher altitude is a climb (with_climbs): no descent
